doubts.claim_under_doubt: Auto-rollback restores the previously-live ref, undoing a bad release.
doubts.disproof_attempt: jelastic_client.deploy_from_git (pre-existing, unmodified by this unit) never re-pins the branch for an environment that already has a VCS project — it only sends `branch` on first-ever creation. On the routine 'push new commits to the same branch, CI redeploys' cycle, previous_ref already equals the branch being deployed, so auto-rollback has no distinct commit to name and cannot actually undo the new commits that broke the deploy.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Either implement commit-level rollback (a versioning/tagging scheme) or document the branch-name-granularity limitation so operators know when auto-rollback has nothing to restore.
doubts.resolution: Documented as a known limitation in skills/deploy/references/non-interactive-release.md rather than fixed — commit-level rollback needs a materially bigger design than this unit's scope. The skip-reason message at the call site was reworded (see finding #6) to stop implying nothing was missed when this gap is hit.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: A failed smoke check reliably indicates the release is unhealthy and should trigger an auto-rollback.
doubts.disproof_attempt: With no polling deadline configured (neither --profile nor --smoke-max-wait), smoke_test.py makes exactly one fixed-timeout attempt — its own docstring warns 'a fifteen-second start-up gets reported as a failed release and triggers a rollback nobody needed'. A single attempt is not a reliable enough signal to justify an automatic host mutation.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Skip auto-rollback (with a clear reason) unless a polling deadline was actually configured, since only then has the smoke check given the app a real chance to come up.
doubts.resolution: verify_and_maybe_roll_back now checks policy.max_wait is None and skips auto-rollback with rollback_skipped_reason naming the gap. New test test_smoke_failure_skips_rollback_when_no_deadline_is_configured; smoke_max_wait added to the existing rollback-triggering tests so they still exercise the rollback path.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: release.py is safe to wire into an automated CI pipeline without additional guardrails.
doubts.disproof_attempt: Nothing in release()'s original signature distinguished dev from prod. A CI job configured with a PROD env_name would perform an auto-rollback-capable PROD deploy with zero human confirmation, violating the constitution's PROD-is-ASK-FIRST invariant, which this agent-free entry point has no built-in way to honour (it cannot show an AskUserQuestion).
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Require an explicit target argument with no default, and refuse target=prod unless an explicit confirm_prod flag (sourced from something upstream that can actually ask a human) is set.
doubts.resolution: release() now requires a keyword-only target ('dev'/'prod', no default) plus confirm_prod; target='prod' without confirm_prod=True refuses before any host contact. CLI gained matching --target (required, choices=[dev,prod]) and --confirm-prod flags. New tests: test_an_unrecognised_target_is_refused_before_contacting_the_host, test_a_prod_release_is_refused_without_explicit_confirmation, test_a_prod_release_proceeds_once_confirmed.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: release.py can be safely invoked from CI for every push without additional coordination.
doubts.disproof_attempt: There is no lock across the whole gate->deploy->smoke->rollback sequence. Two concurrent release.py invocations against the same env_name could interleave their deploy/rollback calls, each unaware of the other's in-flight mutation.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Add a per-env_name lock spanning the whole sequence, or explicitly document that callers must serialize releases per environment upstream.
doubts.resolution: Documented as a known limitation in non-interactive-release.md, matching rollback.py's own pre-existing unlocked assumption — a real cross-invocation lock needs a materially bigger design than this unit's scope. Callers are expected to serialize releases per environment via CI/campaign convention.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: A rollback_triggered: true result with rollback.success: true means the environment is healthy again.
doubts.disproof_attempt: rollback_git only confirms the ref PIN was accepted (or, at best, read back as matching) — it does not itself confirm the application is actually serving traffic on that ref. Nothing in the reported payload distinguished 'restored to a known-good ref' from 'restored to an unverified ref that still isn't answering requests'.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Re-run the smoke check against the restored ref after a successful rollback and surface the result distinctly from the pin confirmation.
doubts.resolution: After a successful rollback_git call, release_rollback re-runs smoke_test.run_smoke_test against the restored ref and adds rollback_health_check / rollback_verified_healthy to the result. New test test_a_recovered_rollback_is_confirmed_healthy_by_the_recheck covers the healthy case; the existing auto-rollback test now asserts rollback_verified_healthy is False when the mock keeps reporting failure.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The rollback_skipped_reason 'no distinct previous ref to restore — nothing to roll back to' accurately communicates the situation to an operator.
doubts.disproof_attempt: That wording reads as reassuring — as if there truly is nothing to restore — when it is actually surfacing the branch-vs-commit granularity gap (finding #1): a live regression from this deploy's own new commits could still be unrestored, because auto-rollback only sees branch names, not commits.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Reword the message to name the actual gap instead of implying nothing was missed.
doubts.resolution: Reworded to 'no distinct previous ref at branch-name granularity ... a live regression from this deploy's new commits may still be unrestored', pointing at the 'Known limitations' section of non-interactive-release.md.
